chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was there and there was nothing other than Him. He always knew what would come into being, so His knowledge of it before it came into being is like His knowledge of it after it came into being.

key_terms.كَوْنٌ: Coming into being, existence, or creation

ai.seo_question: What does Shia theology say about God's knowledge of future events?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine attribute of knowledge (ilm), asserting that Allah's knowledge of future events is identical in nature to His knowledge of existing events, emphasizing His eternal and unchanging awareness prior to creation. In Shia kalām, this distinction refutes the notion that divine knowledge is temporal or acquired, affirming that God's knowing is an essential, non-compositional attribute rather than a change in His essence. It underscores the concept of 'Ilm al-Dhati' (Essential Knowledge), where the Creator's awareness of all potentialities and actualities is simultaneous and complete from eternity.
